name: Vuk Herrera-Kyei
role: Prototype theft and corporate tech acquisition — tech retriever
location: Old Harbor — repurposed shipping infrastructure turned black market hub
description:
Vuk Herrera-Kyei is tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 31, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct ne — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Her entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. She works as a tech retriever out of Old Harbor, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Vuk Herrera-Kyei operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.

core_fears: That their reputation is built on luck, not skill, and the luck is finite
Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
core_desires: Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
coping_mechanisms: Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
blind_spots: Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
psychology.secret: Vuk Herrera-Kyei once worked for corporate intelligence and still has a handler who calls in favors. Each favor erodes what's left of their independence.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
verbal_tics: Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
Calls money 'weight' — as in 'that job doesn't carry enough weight'
example_lines: "Corporate R&D security is built to stop amateurs. I'm a professional."
"The prototype is worth more than both our lives combined. Handle it carefully."
"I steal things that haven't been invented yet. The future is always in transit."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Vuk Herrera-Kyei's reputation — and a price for silence
A corporate black site Vuk Herrera-Kyei once infiltrated is being reopened, and the people inside know her face
Vuk Herrera-Kyei is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
narrative_function: Vuk Herrera-Kyei is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When she makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of her stories.
augmentations: Neural interface jack at base of skull — standard runner-grade, allows direct net access. Internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immune to gas attacks
daily_life: Keeps a rigid daily structure — wake, train, check contracts, maintain gear, sleep. The structure is a defense against the chaos of the work. Deviations from the schedule are a warning sign that something is wrong.

weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions

decision_rules: Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
escalation_ladder: 2. Evade — avoid the problem entirely if possible
3. Misdirect — create a distraction, redirect attention
4. Disable — targeted takedowns, quiet and efficient
5. Eliminate — when silence is no longer an option
6. Vanish — disappear completely, burn identity if necessary

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
habits: Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
breaking_points: Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
Being forced to choose between a crew member and the mission — and choosing wrong
